newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Explosion hits OSCE hotel in Serb part of Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Explosion hits OSCE hotel in Serb part of Bosnia.

text.p: An explosion damaged cars and and a hotel used by international monitors in the east Bosnian town of Zvornik overnight but caused no casualties, the Bosnian Serb new agency SRNA said on Monday.
The two kg (four pound) charge was placed under a jeep used by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) and blew out windows in the hotel and a nearby school.
Thre was no immediate claim of responsibility. But Bosnian Serbs have been angered by a crackdown by the international community on suspected war criminals indicted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal.

An indicted former police chief who was killed by NATO troops while resisting arrest last week was buried on Sunday in an elaborate funeral attended by Bosnian Serb leaders in the northern town of Prijedor.

Zvornik, which Serb forces purged of Moslem residents at the start of Bosnia's 1992-95 war, is known as a stronghold of Serb nationalists and is the east Bosnian headquarters of the Bosnian Serb army.
Attacks on NATO-led peacekeepers and international civilian organisations in Bosnia have been relatively rare since the 1995 peace agreement.
